audit_stage: Frozen 2016 bird GPS source and a pre-outcome 2016 CERRA site-weather/x-y support manifest; no source/year/grid/regime/minima modified after reading heights.

source.independent_weather: Open-Meteo ECMWF CERRA ~5km wind_speed_100m at 4 source-defined colony centroids; each UTC day mean wind classified within site×month lower/upper quartile

primary.p_discrete_resolution: (0+1)/(999+1)=0.001. Monte-Carlo significance for predeclared one-sided wind-informative prediction; not strict exact population probability.

posthoc_descriptive_site_check.role: Not an independent site-stratified significance test and not a second biological dataset.
posthoc_descriptive_site_check.source: Published archived individual-id -> study-site metadata (2016 target source)

supported: Within this tracked Larus fuscus study, calendar-day broad wind regime is associated with repeatable variation in the shape of individually centred vertical flight-use distributions, conditional on the same 5km horizontal cell.
Conditioned vs wind-pooled models predict exactly the same day-heldout GPS fixes for each individual; the observed gain exceeds 999 site-grid/month-block wind-date randomizations.
The effect is not merely a fixed altitude offset of birds; within-bird daily median subtraction removes fixed offsets.
not_supported: Causal wind forcing was identified (unmeasured date conditions or tag errors could generate associations).
CERRA at the colony measures physical winds actually experienced by each bird at every flight point.
Flight mode (flapping/soaring) was measured in this Zeebrugge test; selection was a 5-55 m/s ground-speed proxy.
The 4 colony groups constitute 4 independent study replications.
A universal animal law or convergence with penguin breeding-site concentration was tested.
interpretation.next: Independent year/site/cross-taxon test with prespecified device/behavior diagnostics, before generalizing context-dependent vertical shape beyond this species.
